Phase 37 implemented on branch phase-37-cockpit-launchpad (findings: docs/phases/cockpit-launchpad-lead-conversation-findings.md; every in-cycle gate recorded there). Suite 969 passed / 5 skipped. Version 3.1.0.

Delivered against the approved plan (round 5):
- A. `tagteam serve` bare = cockpit (loopback); `--theme saloon` byte-identical to the pre-3.1 bare page (identity test retargeted); banner "Tagteam cockpit — <project> — <phase · type · rN · state | no active cycle> → URL". Port exclusion = real bind + project-independent port lease (`~/.tagteam/ports/<port>.json`, pid+identity, O_EXCL, released on shutdown incl. SIGTERM, stale=dead pid or definitive identity mismatch, unverifiable=held) + pre-bind connect probe for the loopback/wildcard shadow; holder named only from a verified lease or `/api/info` app:tagteam (added to cockpit/saloon/hub); observed live against the arbiter's stray 3.0.0 servers on 8080.
- Turn slot: `headless.claim_turn_slot/update_turn_slot/release_turn_slot/slot_status` under dualwrite.writer_lock (claim only), owner_token, existing marker keys retained + kind/conversation fields, owner-only unlink, definitive-only recovery (fail closed on unverifiable/legacy); wired into HeadlessEngine._run_attempt (Busy → tick declined, engine.slot_busy), the briefer (Busy → refused), and the watcher's headless tick which re-dispatches the still-owed turn once the slot frees (mock-safe); watcher_status is kind-aware.
- B. `launch.launch_intent` (the plan's matrix; `roadmap.is_terminal_status` normalizes Complete/✅/Absorbed/Deferred/Superseded and `get_incomplete_phases` uses it — regression on a copy of this repo's roadmap), `start_payload` gated on HeadlessEngine.validate(), composite `launch` with a persisted `launches` claim (UNIQUE key = sha256(command+observed), owner pid/ident, attempt, per-step refs, partial JSON) claimed under a short lock, side effects outside (start_watcher: detached --pidfile, ≤5 s pidfile-or-early-exit; the lead's first conversation turn), repeat → existing, concurrent → one insert, orphaned pending reconciled on start/request, retry:true = atomic failed→pending attempt+1 rerunning only missing steps (alive watcher reused, existing turn returned, persisted conversation reused); stop_watcher (identity-checked pidfile only), start_session (manual returns commands). Endpoints: GET /api/start; POST /api/start/launch (the legacy Saloon keeps /api/launch), /api/watch/start|stop, /api/session/start; Start card, watcher chip Start/Stop, approved-state intent, empty-state reason.
- C. `lead_chat`: conversations under .tagteam/conversations/<c-12hex>/ (transcript.md, <n>.log, <n>.events.jsonl), DB v7 (conversations, conversation_turns incl. reply/continuity, launches, usage.kind; NON_FILE_BACKED_TABLES parent-before-child); `send` = one adapter turn with the lead's headless spec (claude --session-id/--resume; codex `build_conversation_argv` → exec --json -C root <policy> --skip-git-repo-check resume <id> - when `codex_resume_supported()` probes true, else budgeted transcript replay; runtime resume failure → failed turn, never replayed), slot kind=conversation, usage kind=conversation, running→ok|failed|cancelled, no pause marker on failure, `reconcile` orphaned running rows on server start and `tagteam lead --list`, `cancel` via bind_inflight, `turn_events` with ids <n>:<seq>/<n>:end replayable from a cursor. Server: GET /api/lead, /api/lead/<cid>, /api/lead/<cid>/events (Last-Event-ID / ?after= replay then live), POST /api/lead/new, /send (202; 409 busy with reason while a cycle turn holds the slot; 413 >32 KB; 400 empty; dry-run), /cancel; ids regex+DB-validated before any path join, path containment asserted. UI: Lead tab first, DOM via createElement/textContent only (JS-source guard + browser check with hostile markup: rendered as text, title unchanged, zero injected elements), composer states idle/sending/busy(+interject)/error, per-conversation SSE with cursor. CLI twin `tagteam lead "msg" [--new] [--conversation ID] [--json] / --list` (exit 3 busy).
- D. Hub rows carry the same intent (read-only, prefetched inputs, no DB); `Start →` (plan/implementation) only when intent.command exists → /p/<id>/#start; hub adds no POSTs.
- E. README ("Talk to the lead, launch, watch and steer"; ladder ③ label + SVG updated together; new cockpit-lead.png), HTW (#cockpit default/lease/launchpad table, new #lead, hub/saloon/files rows), manifest (recipe + 4th screenshot), showcase sentence; pyproject + CITATION 3.1.0.
- F. tests/test_lead_chat.py (18) + tests/test_launchpad.py (17): slot claim/release/owner-only/definitive recovery/fail-closed/barrier race; argv shapes + codex parser smoke + probe cache; chat e2e with resume argv assertions, codex replay/resume, refuse-while-cycle-turn + marker kind, failed turn no pause, orphan reconcile, events replay/cursor, id/size boundaries, not-configured; roadmap terminal normalization on this repo's roadmap; watcher slot re-dispatch; intent matrix incl. exhausted/not-set-up/paused/skip-by-name; headless gate; idempotent launch; concurrent barrier (one watcher, one message); watcher early-exit + partial + retry reuse; three crash windows reconciled+retryable; SSE fast-finish/reconnect/after-end; busy 409 + boundaries + 413 + dry-run; hostile reply round-trip + no-innerHTML guard; watch/session/launch endpoints + legacy /api/launch untouched; port lease both orders/stale/unverifiable/foreign token; serve refusal (unrelated → generic, Tagteam holder named) + immediate restart; hub rows; CLI. conftest isolates the lease dir for every test.

Gates (findings): user walk-through on the seeded idle project (Start card with the exact intent, all three buttons, headless primary because validate() passed; Lead panel with a two-turn conversation; watcher chip Start) captured as docs/media/screenshots/cockpit-lead.png (1280×800, token/paths absent); real `claude -p` conversation on this repo via `tagteam lead` — second message resumed the session (the lead restated the first), transcript + logs on disk, two usage rows kind=conversation, slot free after; hostile markup rendered as text in the browser; port refusal observed live; SIGTERM releases the lease.

Deviations noted for you: composite route is /api/start/launch (legacy Saloon owns /api/launch); conversation_turns gained reply/continuity columns (additive); Playwright hostile check done by hand + JS-source guard in the suite (Playwright is not a test dependency); start_session stubbed in the endpoint test (no terminals in CI); the seed installs the skill contract so Start headless is offered in captures.

The focused Phase 37 suites pass (`35 passed`), and the implementation covers most of the approved plan. Four lifecycle/security bugs remain:

1. `portlease.acquire()` can grant the same port lease twice. It creates the final path with `O_EXCL` and only then writes JSON; a contender that arrives in that window gets `read_lease() is None`, treats the in-progress file as corrupt/stale, unlinks it, and creates its own lease. I reproduced this deterministically by blocking the first `json.dump`: both callers returned `Lease` objects with different tokens and no error. Publish a complete record atomically (or otherwise make the atomic placeholder authoritative); never unlink an unreadable/malformed existing lease merely because it cannot yet be parsed. A bounded reread may accommodate an in-progress writer, but unresolved/unverifiable metadata must fail closed with an actionable message. Add a barrier test at the create-before-write window proving exactly one winner, plus a malformed-record fail-closed test.

2. `lead_chat.send()` does not own cleanup for its full post-claim lifecycle. If `db.add_conversation_turn()` or `_append_transcript()` raises after `claim_turn_slot()`, execution never reaches the runner's `finally`, leaving a conversation marker owned by the still-live server forever. I injected an `add_conversation_turn` failure and confirmed `.tagteam/turns/inflight.json` remained. Conversely, if the injected runner raises an unexpected exception (anything other than `SpawnError`), the marker is released but the DB turn remains `running`; I reproduced that too. Because its owner PID is the still-live cockpit server, reconciliation fails closed and cannot repair it. Wrap everything after the claim in owner-token-safe cleanup, and ensure every created turn reaches `ok|failed|cancelled` even for unexpected setup/runner/persistence exceptions. Tests should inject failure before the row, after the row, in transcript creation, and a non-`SpawnError` runner exception; assert the slot is free and no turn remains `running`.

3. Composite Start is synchronous across the entire agent turn. `server.py:901` calls `launch.launch()` directly; `launch()` calls synchronous `lead_chat.send()`; and the UI does not open the Lead tab/connect its per-conversation SSE until the POST's `onDone`. A real turn can therefore hold the Start request for up to 30 minutes, and the promised `/handoff start` streaming is only shown after completion. Split turn acceptance from execution: claim the slot and persist the running turn/reference, start the agent on a worker, return `202 {conversation_id, turn_n}` promptly, keep the launch claim pending/finalize it from the worker, and make duplicate/retry requests return the same persisted reference. Update the UI to open the Lead panel immediately. Add a blocking-runner endpoint test proving the POST returns while the turn is still `running`, SSE emits before release, completion finalizes the turn/launch, and a concurrent repeat creates neither a second watcher nor message.

4. The approved 64 KiB request-body boundary is absent. `_read_json_body()` trusts `Content-Length` and reads the entire body; only the 32 KiB `text` field is checked afterward. Enforce the cockpit JSON-body cap before reading and return 413 (while retaining the 32 KiB message cap). Test a >64 KiB object whose `text` itself is small, plus malformed/negative length handling, so ignored fields cannot bypass the memory boundary.

Please fix these paths, rerun the focused and full suites, update the findings with the new regression evidence, and resubmit.

Round 2 — the four lifecycle/security bugs (findings "Round 2"; suite 977 passed / 5 skipped):

1. Port lease publish is atomic: the complete record is written to a private temp file in the lease dir and `os.link`ed into place (FileExistsError = held; O_EXCL + single-write fallback only where hard links are unavailable), so a contender never sees a half-written lease. An unreadable/malformed lease is re-read a few times (bounded) and then FAILS CLOSED with an actionable message ("port N has an unreadable lease at <path> — remove it if no tagteam server is running, or use --port N+1"); it is never unlinked because it cannot be parsed. Tests: barrier race at the publish window (os.link blocked until both contenders wrote their record) → exactly one Lease, loser gets PortHeld naming the winner; malformed lease → PortHeld and the file kept byte-for-byte.

2. `lead_chat.send` owns its whole post-claim lifecycle: split into `start_turn` (validate → continuity → claim slot → `running` row → marker fields; any failure after the claim releases the slot and, if the row already exists, ends it `failed: setup failed …`) and `run_turn` (spawn + finalize; slot released in `finally`; an unexpected non-SpawnError runner exception ends the row `failed: runner error …` and re-raises; a failure while finalizing ends it `failed: finalize failed …`); `send` = start_turn + run_turn. Tests inject failure before the row (add_conversation_turn), after the row (_append_transcript), a non-SpawnError runner exception, and a finalize exception — asserting the slot is free, no turn stays `running`, and the conversation is usable again; plus a start_turn/run_turn split test.

3. Start and Send are asynchronous: `POST /api/lead/<cid>/send` calls `start_turn` synchronously (slot claimed, running row + turn number persisted; a Busy answers 409 right there) and runs `run_turn` on a worker, returning 202 {conversation_id, turn_n}. The composite `launch(background=True)` (the server's default) does the same after the watcher step: start_turn, persist conversation_id/turn_n on the launches row, return 202 pending immediately; the worker finalizes the row (succeeded, or failed with the reason if run_turn raised); a repeat while pending returns 202 with the same persisted reference; a repeat after completion returns 200 existing. UI already opens the Lead tab and subscribes the per-conversation SSE from `onDone` on the 202. Test with a slow fake agent: the POST returns in <1.5 s while the turn is `running` and the slot is held (kind=conversation); SSE emits `line` frames before release; a concurrent repeat returns the same conversation_id (one watcher start, one message); completion finalizes the turn (ok, reply) and the launch (repeat → 200 existing, still one turn).

4. 64 KiB body cap: `_read_json_body` checks Content-Length BEFORE reading in cockpit mode (>65536 → 413 "request body exceeds 65536 bytes"; malformed/negative → 400) and the legacy routes under cockpit mode get the same pre-read check; the 32 KiB `text` cap remains. Tests: >64 KiB object with a small `text` → 413 and no turn created; `/api/state` under cockpit → 413; `Content-Length: abc` / `-5` → 400 without reading; small bodies unaffected.

Round 2 fixes the original four findings, and the focused suites pass (`43 passed`). Two async-boundary bugs remain:

1. Failure to start the worker thread strands the accepted turn. Both `launch.launch(background=True)` and the `/api/lead/<cid>/send` route call `start_turn()` first, then call `Thread.start()` without a cleanup guard. If `Thread.start()` raises (for example, process/thread resource exhaustion), no worker owns the `TurnHandle`. I injected `RuntimeError("cannot start thread")` into the composite path and confirmed all three records were stranded: the conversation slot remained held by the live server, the turn stayed `running`, and the launch stayed `pending`; reconciliation cannot clear any of them because the owner PID is alive. Add an explicit `abort_turn(handle, reason)` (or equivalent owner-safe primitive) that releases only the handle's token and terminalizes its row, call it on dispatch failure in both endpoints, and fail the launch claim truthfully. Add regression tests for both composite Start and ordinary Send with `Thread.start` raising: response is an error, slot is free, turn is failed, launch is failed where applicable, and a subsequent send/retry works.

2. A normal failed agent turn is marked as a successful composite launch. `run_turn()` returns a terminal row for expected failures (`SpawnError`, timeout, nonzero exit, cancellation); it raises only for unexpected failures. The launch worker ignores the returned row and unconditionally writes `launches.status='succeeded'`. The synchronous `send=` path likewise marks success regardless of `turn['status']`, and the existing-turn retry path marks any referenced turn succeeded even when its status is `failed` or `cancelled`. Make launch finalization depend on the persisted turn status: only `ok` succeeds; `failed`/`cancelled` produce a failed launch with the turn reference/error in `partial`; `running` remains pending. Preserve at-most-once messaging when retry encounters an existing failed turn, but do not relabel that failed operation as success. Add background and synchronous nonzero/timeout/cancel tests plus reconciliation/retry coverage proving the launch and turn statuses agree and no duplicate message is sent.

The atomic lease publication, fail-closed malformed lease, full post-claim turn cleanup, prompt 202/SSE path, and 64 KiB pre-read body cap otherwise look correct. Fix these two paths, rerun focused/full suites, update findings, and resubmit.
